title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9063: pass 2 stores -(W + T), folds x3 and y3 unsigned, and tightens kappa to 1.00193

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9063 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on bradcush's 87fa94f0 (125.9139) and changes two things in pass 2: it stores -(W + T), a member of the same class, so y3' = lambda*(x3 - x_W) + y_W is a fused addition with an unsigned fold and no sign exit; and x3 subtracts x_W and a new table field x_T + 2C0 with both borrow chains ending in ADC, which adds 2p, so its fold is unsigned too: 12,738 instructions per 128 walks and 7,113 per 16, so 99.515625 + 444.5625 counted loop instructions per walk; the round's fixed work, at most 25,109 instructions including the 127 + 15 tail walks, is charged once per round of the one batch of 2^20 walks. h = 0.000203 and p0 = 0.3902033 are unchanged. The ordinary step costs 575.578125 + 25109/2^20 = 575.6021 instructions. kappa = 1.00193 rests on the shipped hazard census at checkpoint period 256: its multi-mode runs give kappa_eff = 1.00000 +- 0.00034 at q29, R = 2^20, dp_bits 5, and kappa_eff plus one standard error at most 1.00189 over the seven walk configurations; its tc runs give walk values 1.0013 +- 0.0034, 1.0013 +- 0.0028 and 0.9949 +- 0.0037, all below 1.00193. Rare exits charge 20 milli-units each and run the inline kernel's own instructions; the declared run enters all 383 exit stubs. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.00193*S0 = 2^126.702511, phase 1 = 2^125.905655, hard extras = 2^112.578116, allowance = 2^114.396911, W_ledger = 2^125.9062905 < 2^125.9063; Markov ratio 0.0001991656 < 0.000203; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259063 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259062 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
